newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends slightly lower vs dlr.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends slightly lower vs dlr.

text.p: --------------------------- Dec 13 ------------------------- * Peso breaches $26.30 psychological level, then recovers

The Philippine peso ended marginally lower at 26.298 against the dollar from Thursday's close of 26.297, taking its cue from a series of adjustments made by the Central Bank on its selling rate, traders said.
The Central Bank raised its selling rate to 26.301 in the afternoon from 26.295 in the morning. Dealers were unsure of the reasons for the shift.

"Banks just followed the Central Bank's selling rate," one trader said, adding that buyers panicked slightly when the bank posted its rate at 26.301. The Central Bank sold more than $30 million at 26.301, but the rate then settled at 26.298.

Banks were mainly net buyers of dollars to take advantage of a two-day arbitrage play. Trades done in the Philippine dealing system are settled the next trading day. Banks which buy dollars on Fridays keep their pesos until Monday and earn higher interest rates over the weekend.
A total of $178.55 million was traded, higher than yesterday's $109 million.
